samples.summary: Google provider registration is decided at module *import* time, before ConfigModule loads `.env` — a `.env`-configured deployment gets a 500 on /auth/google instead of a working login
samples.evidence: `const googleProviders = googleAuthConfigured() ? [GoogleStrategy] : [];` (packages/backend/src/auth/auth.module.ts:37) runs when the module file is evaluated. `packages/backend/src/app.module.ts:6` imports AuthModule at the top of the file, i.e. before the decorator argument at `app.module.ts:29` (`ConfigModule.forRoot({ isGlobal: true })`) executes and dotenv assigns the file's variables into `process.env`; `packages/backend/src/main.ts` loads no env itself. The documented backend config channel is a `.env` file in the package (`packages/backend/README.md:18` "Create a `.env` file in this package", with the new GOOGLE_* block at README.md:44-47). So with GOOGLE_* in `.env`, `GoogleStrategy` is never registered, yet `GoogleAuthGuard.canActivate` (google-auth.guard.ts) and `AuthController.authProviders()` (auth.controller.ts:240) read `process.env` at *request* time, after dotenv ran — they report Google as configured and let the request through to `AuthGuard('google')`, which throws passport's "Unknown authentication strategy" 500. The login page will also show the Google button. Note the boot warning in the same file (auth.module.ts:74-82) runs in the constructor, i.e. *after* ConfigModule, so it will disagree with the provider list and stay silent. Fix belongs on the new code: decide provider registration with the same timing the guard uses (e.g. register the strategy unconditionally behind a lazily-constructed factory, or read env after ConfigModule).

samples.summary: The login design-sandbox scene now makes an unmocked `/auth/providers` request, which the frame's fetch kill-switch reports as a hard scene failure
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/login/page.tsx:29` adds `fetchAuthProviders()` on mount, which does a raw `fetch(`${VITE_BACKEND_API_URL}/auth/providers`)` (packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:153-155). The login scene is `packages/design-sandbox/scenes.config.json:104-118` with `mocks: ["theme","router"]` and no `fixtures`, so `fixturesFor` (packages/design-sandbox/src/scenes/fixtures/index.ts:72) yields an empty table — and `AUTH_FIXTURES` (fixtures/auth.ts:41, which the login scene does not even declare) has no `/api/auth/providers` entry. `installFetchGuard` calls `onMiss` and throws on any unmatched URL (packages/design-editor/src/scenes/fetch-fixtures.ts:267-274), and `packages/design-sandbox/scripts/verify-scenes.mjs:375` fails the scene on `misses.length !== 0`. `fetchAuthProviders`'s try/catch swallows the thrown error for rendering, but the `wb:error`/`kind:'fetch'` report to the host has already fired (verify-scenes.mjs:297-312), so the login scene check now fails. Fix: add the provider fixture to the login scene's table.

samples.evidence: packages/frontend/README.md:122 — `│   ├── login-form.tsx        # GitHub OAuth button`, now out of step with packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx, which renders GitHub *and* a conditional Google button driven by the new `googleEnabled` prop.

verdict.reason: Verified the claimed code and the timing chain. auth.module.ts:37 evaluates googleAuthConfigured() as a module-body statement, i.e. before its own decorator argument (ConfigModule.forRoot() at auth.module.ts:41) and before app.module.ts:29's ConfigModule.forRoot({isGlobal:true}) — app.module.ts:6 requires AuthModule first. A repo-wide grep for `ConfigModule.forRoot|dotenv` finds only those two call sites; main.ts loads no env and package.json's start scripts have no dotenv preload. googleAuthConfigured() reads process.env (oauth-providers.ts:25,38), so on a .env-configured install (documented at README.md:18 and README.md:44-47; docker-compose.yaml:65 points `pnpm dev` at packages/backend/.env) GoogleStrategy is not registered, while two consumers outside that decision re-read process.env at request time and disagree: google-auth.guard.ts:22,39,45 lets the request through to AuthGuard('google') with no registered strategy (passport "Unknown authentication strategy" 500), and auth.controller.ts:240 reports google:true so the login page shows the button. The in-file boot warning (auth.module.ts:74-82) runs in the constructor, after ConfigModule, so it stays silent and cannot flag the inconsistency. No guard, preload, or earlier env load removes the mismatch, so the finding is real and blocking under the blast-radius rubric (a broken/wrongly-reporting site in code the changed module's decision does not show).

verdict.reason: The claimed gap is real and I could find no counterexample. The login page's new mount effect (packages/frontend/src/app/login/page.tsx:29) calls fetchAuthProviders, which issues a raw fetch to `${VITE_BACKEND_API_URL}/auth/providers` (packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:150-155). In the sandbox, VITE_BACKEND_API_URL is defined as http://scene.invalid/api (packages/design-sandbox/vite.config.ts:164,189), so the guard keys it as pathname /api/auth/providers (packages/design-editor/src/scenes/fetch-fixtures.ts:117-134). The login scene declares mocks ["theme","router"] with no shell and no fixtures (packages/design-sandbox/scenes.config.json:104-118), and fixturesFor merges only SHELL_FIXTURES (shell==='app'), BY_MOCK['auth'] and BY_FIXTURE_REF refs (packages/design-sandbox/src/scenes/fixtures/index.ts:72-81) — so its table is empty. AUTH_FIXTURES itself contains only /api/auth/me and /api/notifications/unread-count (packages/design-sandbox/src/scenes/fixtures/auth.ts:41-56), and a repo-wide grep for auth/providers turns up no fixture entry in any package. No baseline table is merged at install time (packages/design-editor/src/scenes/scene-entry.tsx:159-175), and the guard's passthrough list covers only same-origin Vite/editor/debug-report paths (fetch-fixtures.ts:234-244), so the request reaches onMiss + throw (fetch-fixtures.ts:267-274). onMiss posts wb:error kind:'fetch', which verify-scenes captures into __wbMisses and fails the scene on (packages/design-sandbox/scripts/verify-scenes.mjs:307-316,374-375); `login` is a live, non-deferred scene (packages/design-sandbox/test/scenes/manifest.test.ts:146-159). The try/catch in fetchAuthProviders only suppresses the render-side error — the miss report has already fired. This is exactly the blast-radius case: a site outside the diff (the sandbox login scene and its verify gate) that the change breaks.
